chunks: My father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to me, from Hammad ibn Ya'la ibn Hammad, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa al-Juhani, from Hurayz ibn Abdullah, from Zurarah ibn A'yan, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The believer's amusement is in three things: enjoying his women, joking around with his brethren, and praying at night.
ai.seo_question: What are the three things in which a believer finds amusement according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith as a counterbalance to asceticism, affirming that spiritual devotion includes legitimate worldly pleasures within the framework of Sharia. The triad of marital intimacy, social camaraderie, and night prayer reflects the Shia emphasis on a holistic life where the body and soul are both nurtured, preventing religious burnout through balanced enjoyment.
